Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 103, verses 1–3:

﴿By al-ʿAṣr (the time/afternoon)﴾. Regarding it there are three opinions. The first is that it is the afternoon prayer (ṣalat al-ʿaṣr), by which God swore because of its excellence. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever misses the afternoon prayer, it is as if he has lost his family and his wealth." The second is that it is the late part of the day (al-ʿashiyy), by which He swore just as He swore by the forenoon (al-ḍuḥā). This is supported by the statement of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb: "I asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about al-ʿaṣr, and he said: 'Your Lord swears by the end of the day.'" The third is that it is time in general (al-zamān).

﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾. Al-insān (mankind) is a genus noun, and for this reason He made an exception from it: ﴿except for those who have believed﴾, so it is a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil).

﴿And advise one another to truth﴾, i.e., they enjoined one another to the truth and to patience. So al-ḥaqq (the truth) is Islam and what it entails, and in this there is an indication of the falsehood of the disbelievers. And in patience there is an indication of the patience of the believers in bearing the harm the disbelievers inflicted upon them in Mecca.
